title: Been working on East Bank some more. Getting the bots and destruction right has been harder than I expected
author: Affectionate_Tie6915
selftext:
I've posted about East Bank here a couple times already, but I've been working on it some more and figured I'd share where it's at now.

For anyone who hasn't seen it, it's basically a browser FPS with a destructible city. You can drive tanks around, get into shootouts with bots, blow up buildings, pull off heists, etc. There's also multiplayer, co-op, and a nighttime stealth mission.

I've been using Claude for pretty much all the coding. Fable 5.2 Ultra Code handled most of the initial foundation, and then I went through a couple more iterations to fix smaller issues and polish things up.

One thing I've noticed is that getting the initial version working is actually pretty straightforward. It's everything after that which gets complicated. I'd change one mechanic, somehow break three other things, and then spend way too much time figuring out what went wrong. Especially with the physics and bots, there's still quite a bit I want to improve.

But yeah, this is where it's at currently. It's completely free btw and runs directly in your browser, so no downloads or anything.

[https://eastbank.fly.dev/](https://eastbank.fly.dev/)

If anyone gets a chance to try it, I'd be interested in hearing what you think. Especially what feels off or what you'd improve first.

Also curious if anyone else working on larger games with Claude has run into similar issues where fixing one system ends up breaking a bunch of unrelated stuff.

comments.author: Alarmed-Quail7617
comments.body: Using fable 5.2 and ultra code for coding is quite a waste of credits for no real good reason. You can get similar output on opus 5.5 medium for 1/10th the credit cost. The only good thing fable does right now is provide better visual support for blender and other modeling

comments.author: PoleTree
comments.body: Might help with the destruction if you have varying "materials". Right now it just looks like everything inside the explosion disappears. Probably look more natural if things like walls and furniture were destroyed to a greater extent compared to floors/ceilings, pillars, ground/pavement, etc.
